title: Temari thread-ball patterns
summary: Temari are Japanese balls wound with soft stuffing and layered thread, then divided into equal sections by guide threads and decorated with embroidery in bands, stars and flower-like shapes. The same count of divisions makes the pattern repeat evenly all round the ball.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a shape from the tray under the disc.
Touch a segment to stitch it: the same shape appears in the matching segments all round, as the ball is divided into equal parts.
Copy the small ball shown above, then press Check.
rules: The disc shows the ball seen from above its pole, divided into sixteen equal sections; the design repeats four times round.
Each shape you place is copied to its three matching sections in the same band.
A segment counts only when its shape and its colour both match the target; three stars need a nearly perfect copy.
heritageNote: Temari were made in Japan from old silk and thread scraps and are still stitched by hand today, from simple divisions to elaborate designs. The sphere is divided with pins and temporary threads before the final stitches are laid.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original, in the style of the tradition)
